metaDescription: Connellsville was once the coke capital of the world. Its mineral deeds carry that history. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly, cash offer, no broker.
heroLead: Connellsville was called the coke capital of the world a century ago, and the mineral deeds written during that boom still govern who owns what underground here today.
intro: There's a particular kind of paperwork tangle that comes with a place like Connellsville, where an entire regional economy was centered on coal and coke before oil and gas ever entered the picture. Deeds from that era severed coal rights aggressively, and oil and gas were sometimes bundled in with the coal reservation, sometimes carved out separately, sometimes never mentioned at all, which under Pennsylvania law can mean they stayed with the surface owner.
If you own land or an inherited fraction near Connellsville and aren't sure which of those situations applies to you, that's exactly the kind of research we do before making an offer, not after.

sections.heading: The Coke Region's Layered Mineral History
paragraphs: The Connellsville coke region produced some of the most aggressive coal severances in Pennsylvania history, with entire townships sold off to coal and coke companies while surface owners kept farming above. Oil and gas rights sometimes rode along with those coal deeds and sometimes didn't, depending on the exact company and era. Untangling a Connellsville-area chain of title often means reading through several conveyances spanning decades before we can say with confidence what a given family actually owns.
This is patient work, and we do it as part of evaluating your interest, not as a separate cost to you.

sections.heading: Marcellus Interest on the Fringe
paragraphs: Fayette County sits on the flank of the Marcellus wet-gas core, meaning development here has been more selective than in Washington or Greene counties to the west. Connellsville-area acreage has seen some operator interest over the years, but activity depends heavily on the specific section and which company holds the lease, if any. We check recent permitting near your tract before discussing value.

sections.heading: A Straight Answer on What You Own
paragraphs: A lot of families near Connellsville have heard vague stories, that grandpa sold the coal but kept the gas, or that a cousin somewhere has the deed. We'd rather find the actual recorded documents at the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds than rely on family memory alone, and we'll tell you plainly what we find, even if it's not what you expected to hear.

faqs.question: My family's land near Connellsville had the coal sold off long ago. Do we still own oil and gas?
faqs.answer: Possibly, depending on the exact wording of the coal severance. Some old deeds bundled oil and gas with coal, others left them with the surface. We check the actual language.

faqs.question: Is Connellsville in an active drilling area?
faqs.answer: It's on the flank of the Marcellus wet-gas core, so activity is more selective than deeper-core counties. We look at recent permitting near your specific tract.

faqs.question: My family only has vague stories about what was sold. Can you still figure it out?
faqs.answer: Yes. We research the recorded chain of title at the Fayette County Recorder of Deeds rather than relying on family recollection.
